repo_prior_art.cite: eid_snapshot_commonnoise_stabilizer — a covariance fiber project, but not numerical edge-identification complexity for linear SEMs.

published_prior_art.cite: DorflerVanDerZanderBlaserLiskiewicz2024 gives unrestricted promise-∀R membership and PSPACE; GuptaBlaser2024 gives generic randomized polynomial-time tree identification, not an all-covariance numerical fiber algorithm.

DorflerVanDerZanderBlaserLiskiewicz2024 already gives depth-one bipartite instances, bottom/root outdegree one, rational strictly diagonally dominant positive-definite covariance, and a planted 0/1 source solution; maximum directed indegree two remains the proposed strict restriction.

No verified source states a pointwise numerical-edge-identification complexity dichotomy at maximum directed indegree one versus two; the closest results are DorflerVanDerZanderBlaserLiskiewicz2024 and GuptaBlaser2024.
DorflerVanDerZanderBlaserLiskiewicz2024 uses a growing-fan-in storage node; GuptaBlaser2024 treats generic directed trees, neither parameterizes the number of two-parent vertices in numerical fibers.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 2; tldr; project_justification.strict_delta
novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed tightening incorrectly counts depth one, root/bottom outdegree one, and rational strict diagonal dominance as new restrictions: Dörfler et al.'s published reduction already has each of them; retain maximum indegree two as the actual strict delta and separately establish whether an explicitly output planted witness adds anything.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 2; def:compiler; source instance Q
soundness_flags.one_line: “Planted normalized quadratic feasibility,” its yes/no predicate, and the selector convention are not formally defined, so “no-instance of the uncomplemented source” and the claimed many-one reduction have no determined decision problem.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 5–7, Section 4, especially lines 299–302, 361–363, and 396–425; Appendix A.1, Corollary 4.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published construction is already a depth-one bipartite graph with every bottom-layer node of outdegree one, sets unspecified covariance entries to 0 off diagonal and ℓ on diagonal so that Σ is strictly diagonally dominant and positive definite, and reduces complement QUAD++ to numerical edge identification.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1, Abstract and Results; pp. 2 and 6, equations (2)–(3), Algorithm 2, and Theorem 27.
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies directed trees, gives a randomized polynomial-time generic one/two/infinite identification classification, and explicitly notes that generic denominators can vanish at concrete substitutions.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define QUAD++/the planted normalized source as a promise language: state its input encoding, supplied rational planted assignment, selector coordinate, and yes/no condition; then state the reduction against that exact complement.

Rewrite every novelty comparison to Dörfler et al. so the strict improvement is exclusively the maximum-indegree-two, fiber-bijective compiler; drop depth, outdegree-one, rationality, and diagonal-dominance as purported new restrictions unless a genuinely stronger version is specified.

Add a worked small compiled gate instance that lists its graph, covariance, planted coefficient matrix, and the complete projected fiber, making the no-extra-branches assertion independently auditable.

recommended_next_step: Revise the hardness source/problem definition and correct the Dörfler comparison, then return the field-tier fan-in-one/fan-in-two frontier to Stage 0.
